title: Best Online Shopping Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare a tracker blocker, a link cleaner, virtual card numbers and a coupon extension for online shopping privacy, scored on one published rubric.
intro: Online retailers track your behavior to personalize prices and collect personal data. This page compares four tools for shopping privacy (a tracker blocker, a link cleaner, virtual card numbers and a coupon extension) on the same six criteria.

products.name: Privacy Badger
products.tagline: EFF's tracker blocker that stops third parties seen tracking people across sites
pros: Blocks trackers from a list EFF keeps updated by crawling thousands of sites
cons: May break some shopping site features

products.name: Honey
cons: Owned by PayPal, raises privacy concerns
Primary focus on deals, not privacy
Faces lawsuits alleging it takes over creators' affiliate commissions

products.name: Capital One Eno
products.tagline: Virtual card numbers for secure checkout
pros: A virtual number can be limited to one merchant
cons: Requires a Capital One credit card

products.name: ClearURLs
products.tagline: Removes tracking parameters from shopping links
cons: No protection against other tracking methods
Chrome has disabled it until a Manifest V3 version ships; Firefox is unaffected

verdict.summary: Privacy Badger scores highest on these six criteria: it blocks cross-site trackers on every shopping site, though it has no shopping features and doesn't protect card details. ClearURLs is second; it strips tracking parameters from links, but Chrome has disabled its current version, so it is a Firefox tool for now. Capital One Eno is the only tool here that protects your card number, using virtual card numbers, but it needs a Capital One credit card and does nothing about tracking. Honey scores lowest: it finds coupons and tracks prices, but it blocks nothing and collects shopping data itself.

pro_tips: Compare prices in a private window, which starts without your cookies or signed-in session, to see whether a site is showing you a personalized price
Clear cookies and browsing data between shopping sessions to prevent retailers from building detailed profiles
Compare prices across multiple devices or browsers to detect dynamic pricing schemes targeting your specific profile
Use virtual credit card numbers when available to protect your real financial information from data breaches
Enable tracker blocking extensions before starting shopping sessions to prevent cross-site data sharing

faqs.question: Why do online retailers track my shopping behavior?
faqs.answer: Retailers track your behavior to implement dynamic pricing, show personalized ads, build customer profiles, and increase profit margins by charging different prices to different customers based on perceived willingness to pay.

faqs.question: Can I get different prices if I shop in incognito mode?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. Retailers can vary prices by location, device and account history. A private window starts without your cookies or signed-in session, so comparing prices in one can reveal personalized pricing, but it doesn't change your location or IP address.

faqs.question: Are virtual credit cards safe for online shopping?
faqs.answer: Virtual credit cards are very safe and often safer than regular cards. They create unique numbers for each merchant or transaction, so if one gets compromised, your main account remains protected and you can easily cancel the virtual number.

faqs.question: Do privacy tools break shopping website functionality?
faqs.answer: Some privacy tools may occasionally interfere with shopping site features like checkout or account logins. Most modern privacy tools allow you to whitelist trusted sites or temporarily disable protection for specific purchases.

faqs.question: How can I tell if a retailer is using dynamic pricing against me?
faqs.answer: Check prices from different devices, browsers, or locations. Clear your cookies and revisit the site, or use price comparison tools. If prices vary significantly for the same product, dynamic pricing may be in use.
